message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to buy. The fundamentals support a purchase: revenue of $391,035M (up 2% YoY), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and very strong operating cash flow of $118,254M against $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. The reported net income figure in the filing's highlights ($96,995M) reflects pre-State-Aid net income, so I anchored on the audited statement figures; the flat-to-lower net income vs. FY2023 is attributable to a one-time, non-operating $10.2B net tax charge related to the EU State Aid Decision, not to deteriorating operations — gross margin actually improved to 46.2% from 44.1%, driven by Services (+13% to $96,169M at 73.9% margin), which offsets softness in Greater China (-8%) and in iPad/Wearables. Growth is modest and headline risks (DOJ/EU antitrust, DMA) are real, but cash generation and balance-sheet strength justify a measured position. Within the mandate (AAPL only, buy-only, ≤$10,000/order, ≤$20,000/day, limit near market), I placed one buy order: 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00 against a quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68/ask $222.72), a notional of $9,812 — under the per-order cap and well under today's total. The order filled at $223.00, leaving the cash and existing 100 MSFT shares untouched and no money moved out of the account.
